pr_title: Cleanup Android input on render thread settings
pr_body:
Follow up to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/93933 

Clean up the set of settings used to control whether Android input should be dispatched on the render thread.

Addresses comments in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/93933#discussion_r1666071821 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/93933#issuecomment-2210437977

Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94132
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94202

<!--
Please target the `master` branch in priority.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.

To speed up the contribution process and avoid CI errors, please set up pre-commit hooks locally:
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/development/code_style_guidelines.html
-->
pr_comments:
Looks great. I also totally agree with merging the concepts of input buffering and agile flushing since they always work in tandem and that makes things simpler.

My only remaining concern is regarding accumulated input. I think whether it's enabled or nor shouldn't contribute to deciding which thread to send events through. Accumulation works regardless agile flushing is enabled or not since it will use the input buffer regardless. In case agile flushing is enabled, well, it will have fewer chances of merging events, but between flushes it will still accumulate as events come.

> Input events are dispatched on the render thread whenever input buffering is disabled. With the current logic this happens when both accumulated input and agile flushing are disabled, hence why accumulated input is checked prior to deciding where to dispatch the input events.

My point is that sending via the render thread should happen if, and only if, agile input is disabled. Whether accumulation is enabled or not is unrelated. Accumulation just means that events are not parsed directly but added to a buffer and new events can be merged with the last one in the buffer. That works the same regardless which thread sends the events. The only difference is that if agile flushing is enabled (events sent from UI thread), there will be multiple flush points per frame, and if agile is disabled (events from render thread) there will be a single flush.

> My point is that sending via the render thread should happen if, and only if, agile input is disabled. Whether accumulation is enabled or not is unrelated. Accumulation just means that events are not parsed directly but added to a buffer and new events can be merged with the last one in the buffer. That works the same regardless which thread sends the events. The only difference is that if agile flushing is enabled (events sent from UI thread), there will be multiple flush points per frame, and if agile is disabled (events from render thread) there will be a single flush.

Make sense! I've updated the criteria for dispatching on the render thread to only depend on the state of agile input.

> Make sense! I've updated the criteria for dispatching on the render thread to only depend on the state of agile input.

Thinking about it some more, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the new proposed behavior as it'll change the default input dispatch thread..

The previous criteria for dispatching input events from the UI thread was:
 > is there a buffer so that the UI thread doesn't block parsing and routing the input event?

This meant that both `accumulated input` and the default behavior (given input buffering was always enabled on Android) would dispatch input from the UI thread (a bit of a moot point though as there was no alternatives).


The new criteria for dispatching input events from the UI thread is:
> is agile input enabled?

If true, we dispatch from the UI thread, otherwise we dispatch from the render thread.

The change in behavior is that previously, the default configuration (`agile input` **disabled**, `accumulated input` **enabled**) would dispatch from the UI thread. 
With the update, **the default configuration now dispatches from the render thread.** 

The concern here being that I'm leery of changing the default behavior, especially for users that are not seeing an issue with the default configuration.
As such, I'll advocate for the previous approach of conditioning the use of the render thread for dispatch on both `accumulated input` and `agile input` being disabled, as this most closely matches the previous behavior. 

cc @RandomShaper @akien-mga

My notion is that before #93933 input events on Android were delivered via the UI thread uncontionally (moreover, regardless accumulation being enabled or not).

Input buffering was enabled at startup regardless any setting:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e6448ca0aa050b71cb40d9658b7233b8ec7f7382/platform/android/display_server_android.cpp#L654

And then, for instance, when user triggered an input event, this code path woud be followed:
1. `GodotInputHandler.onTouchEvent()` would be the first function under our control getting the event that would then call back to another method of itself:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e6448ca0aa050b71cb40d9658b7233b8ec7f7382/platform/android/java/lib/src/org/godotengine/godot/input/GodotInputHandler.java#L225

2. `GodotInputHandler.handleTouchEvent()` would then invoke the C++ implementation of `dispatchTouchEvent()`:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e6448ca0aa050b71cb40d9658b7233b8ec7f7382/platform/android/java/lib/src/org/godotengine/godot/input/GodotInputHandler.java#L639

3. `Java_org_godotengine_godot_GodotLib_dispatchTouchEvent()` would in turn pass the event to `AndroidInputHandler`:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e6448ca0aa050b71cb40d9658b7233b8ec7f7382/platform/android/java_godot_lib_jni.cpp#L307

4. `AndroidInputHandler::process_touch_event()` would then send the event to `Input` to be parsed there:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e6448ca0aa050b71cb40d9658b7233b8ec7f7382/platform/android/android_input_handler.cpp#L238

All that happens within the UI thread.

> All that happens within the UI thread.

Yeah I agree, my comment was that now the default will be to use the render thread. If we are okay with that then I'm good to go.

Also should we have agile input flushing enabled by default?
Is there a reason why it's disabled by default?

That's a good question. I don't have a strong opinion. If anything, given that it's only implemented on Android, it may be better to have it as opt-in per the least astonishment principle. In the future we should have the same thread split and so agile flushing will be available everywhere. If we ever reach that point, having it as a default would make more sense. But, again, I'm not a big proponent of either way.
Working on one additional set of changes to help limit the creation of `Runnable` objects when dispatching input to the render thread.

> Working on one additional set of changes to help limit the creation of `Runnable` objects when dispatching input to the render thread.

On second thought, I'll do the memory optimizations in a separate PR, so this PR is good to go.

issue_context.title: Running a project from a nonexisting path prints spurious error message about a benchmark key not being found
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.3.dev 82cedc83c9069125207c128f9a07ce3d82c317cc
- Not reproducible in: 4.2.2.stable, 4.3.beta2

### System information

Godot v4.3.beta (82cedc83c) - Fedora Linux 40 (KDE Plasma) - X11 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (nvidia; 550.90.07) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 Threads)

### Issue description

Running the following command (which points to a non-existing folder):

```
bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.x86_64 --path non_existing_folder
```

Results in:

```
ERROR: Benchmark key 'Startup:Core' doesn't exist.
   at: benchmark_end_measure (./core/os/os.cpp:658)
```

Previously, this did not result in that particular error being printed, only the "project not found, aborting" message. That message is still displayed, but there's a spurious error message alongside it now.

I bisected the regression to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/93933. cc @m4gr3d 


### Steps to reproduce

Run this from a command line in the Godot repository root:

```
bin/<godot_executable_name> --path non_existing_folder
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
comments:
On beta 3:
```
% godot --version
4.3.beta.custom_build.82cedc83c
ERROR: Benchmark key 'Startup:Core' doesn't exist.
   at: benchmark_end_measure (./core/os/os.cpp:658)
```

review_comments:
This setting (like input accumulation) is no longer documented in the ProjectSettings class reference, but it still exists. Make sure `GLOBAL_DEF()` is called early enough so that `--doctool` can pick it up. This may require making the `GLOBAL_DEF()` a  standalone expression and using `GLOBAL_GET()` later on. You could also move it to `project_settings.cpp` to centralize its location.

Also, is there much of a point in having *editor* settings for agile event flushing and input accumulation? I can't see much reasons for changing their value from the default. I would just make the editor ignore the project settings to ensure consistency across projects. (Editor plugins can force specific values in the editor if they really need to.)

> Also, is there much of a point in having editor settings for agile event flushing and input accumulation? I can't see much reasons for changing their value from the default. 

For both settings, yes there's value. The editor being itself a Godot Android app, and being expected to run onto a wide variety of Android devices, this allows users to select the options best suited to their devices regardless of the project specific settings. 
And to us devs, this allows to quickly validate any input related changes with either or both of those settings enabled / disabled. For example, I used those editor settings to test the changes in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/93933.

> This setting (like input accumulation) is no longer documented in the ProjectSettings class reference, but it still exists.

It's still documented. `use_input_buffering` and `use_accumulated_input` were the ones removed. Both were introduced in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/93933:
- `use_input_buffering` was deprecated in favor or `agile_event_flushing`
- the `use_accumulated_input` project setting was added in error. I overlooked that the setting is already exposed via [`Input::use_accumulated_input`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_input.html#class-input-property-use-accumulated-input).

> the `use_accumulated_input` project setting was added in error. I overlooked that the setting is already exposed via [Input::use_accumulated_input](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_input.html#class-input-property-use-accumulated-input).

It's indeed already exposed via the Input singleton, but the project setting was added so that you can disable it without needing to use an autoloaded script or something similar. It's similar to project settings like `display/window/size/transparent`.

Some existing projects may rely upon this project setting, so removing it could unexpectedly break them (unless the setting didn't work in its current state). I recall seeing this being a regular topic of discussion on Reddit and forums, so I think it'd be better to provide a fixed version of the setting as opposed to removing it entirely.

> It's indeed already exposed via the Input singleton, but the project setting was added so that you can disable it without needing to use an autoloaded script or something similar. It's similar to project settings like `display/window/size/transparent`.

The project setting was only added in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/93933/files#diff-18b7c19417a461e4793bb2157831659d96ede991391e10ee5bc51f19453b7685 (which has only been included in 4.3 beta 3), and that was mostly because I forgot about the `Input` singleton property. You can check the code prior to that, there's no reference to a project settings for `use_accumulated_input`.
